static_traits.name: Lin Rui
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to confide in, but not yet discussed this anxiety with them; avoiding sugary social situations due to anxiety about sweets, affecting relationships with friends and family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; without similar prior problems or psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, high cooperativeness; able to self-reflect and accept reframing; describing anxiety and guilt specifically, calm tone but with marked anxiety; positive motivation to seek help

basic_info.main_problem: I have a distorted belief that enjoying cupcakes will make me obese and eventually die of heart disease. These beliefs have been bringing me significant anxiety and distress.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent anxiety and distress have begun affecting my daily life and well-being, so I am seeking counseling for guidance and support.
growth_experiences: About six months ago anxiety about sweets began due to health concerns; work and personal life stress made the related thoughts more prominent; since then anxiety appears almost daily, especially during meals or social gatherings; tried countering these thoughts through strict dietary restriction and excessive exercise, but not yet able to relieve anxiety.

core_beliefs: Once my diet is not strict enough, it will bring catastrophic health consequences.
My body is fragile and unsafe, small deviations may also lead to serious illness.

special_situations.event: After eating a cupcake at a friend's party
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat sweets, I am seriously harming my health and significantly increasing the risk of heart disease
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Afterward strictly restricts diet, increases exercise, avoids sugary foods and social occasions with desserts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I made a serious mistake, this will make me fat, and in the end I will have a heart attack.

special_situations.event: Sees sweets (such as cupcakes) at every mealtime
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot completely avoid sweets, it means I lack self-control and my health will spiral out of control
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Makes rigid diet rules, strictly calculates intake, exercises compulsively to 'hedge'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as I eat a little, I will lose control, gain weight, and my health will go downhill.

special_situations.event: Recalling health concerns from six months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Since I have had worries about health problems before, that means my body is more prone to problems, and even a little sweet food could trigger a big problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treating 'zero sweets' as a safety rule, reinforcing dietary control and avoidance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My body cannot withstand any stimulation from sweets, the consequences will be severe.

special_situations.event: Desserts appearing at social gatherings, people around enjoying sweets
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat sweets, something will definitely happen in the future (weight gain, heart disease), it is only a matter of time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social gatherings or deliberately avoiding sweets in the situation to lower anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I take one bite, there will definitely be serious health problems in the future.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to enjoy food and life with peace of mind and to relax comfortably in social settings
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control over body and health, developing serious illness or even death
defense_goal: Reducing uncertainty and anxiety through strict dietary control and excessive exercise
Avoids social occasions with sugar to avoid triggered fear

object_relations.self_representation: A fragile individual who needs a high degree of self-control to maintain safety
object_relations.object_representation: Sweets/social occasions are potential threats and temptations that may bring harm

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When desserts appear at social gatherings or others urge them to eat
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing sweets as a dangerous stimulus that brings serious health consequences ('not even one bite allowed')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Firmly refuses on the grounds of health risks, in a decisive tone, avoiding further discussion of and contact with the related foods.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When intense anxiety and guilt appear after eating sweets
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing current unease to 'sweets have already harmed the body', needing immediate compensation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Immediately arranges high-intensity exercise or formulates a stricter diet plan, speech rate quickens, emphasizing 'must act immediately' to relieve guilt and tension.

manifestations: Directly connecting eating sweets with future heart attacks and death
Feeling strongly threatened by health uncertainty, repeatedly imagining the worst outcome
outcomes: Avoiding socializing and sweets, life restricted

manifestations: Restricting diet and lifestyle with rigid rules, reducing freedom of choice
Gaining a 'sense of control' through excessive exercise
Avoiding social gatherings to avoid contact with sweets
Relationships with friends and family affected
outcomes: Support system not yet fully utilized, increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Enforces 'eating sweets is necessarily harmful' as an absolute rule
Finds evidence for 'moderation is also fine' hard to accept, tending to insist on rigid health rules

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Redirects the craving for sweets into strict constraints on myself: restricting diet, exercising excessively
After anxiety appears, 'compensating' through self-pressure rather than seeking external support

positive_force: Positive help-seeking motivation, willing to try new methods (such as behavioral experiments)
Possessing some rational discernment (admitting 'one sweet will not ruin health')
Having a few close friends who can provide emotional support
Willingness to practice self-observation and cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization are significant
Introjecting 'health = absolute control' as a rigid rule, easily triggering guilt
Maintaining the anxiety cycle through dietary restriction, excessive exercise, and avoiding socializing
Work and personal life stress heighten the sensitivity of health anxiety
Dining and social situations are high-frequency trigger situations, strengthening negative conditioned reflexes

target_behavior.behavior: Intense anxiety and guilt when seeing or eating sweets (especially cupcakes)
antecedent: Recalling health concerns from six months ago
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophically links eating sweets with serious health consequences (weight gain, heart attack), amplified by prior health worries and stress
target_behavior.function: Avoiding anticipated health threats and lowering anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Persistently high anxiety and guilt, impaired eating experience, decreased quality of life

target_behavior.behavior: Strict dietary restriction and excessive exercise (compensatory behaviors)
antecedent: Feeling intense unease after eating sweets
When thoughts of possibly 'losing control' or 'getting fat' appear
target_behavior.core_reason: Hedges catastrophizing beliefs through extreme control, seeking a sense of certainty and security
target_behavior.function: Gaining a subjective sense of control and relieving anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Reinforcing the 'sweets = danger' conditioned reflex, maintaining and intensifying the anxiety cycle

antecedent: Being invited to gatherings or celebrations with desserts
Anticipating it will be hard to avoid sweets at the venue
target_behavior.core_reason: Believing that contact with sweets will inevitably lead to serious consequences, thus lowering the threat through avoidance
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships damaged, reduced social support, negative beliefs not reality-tested
